title: Subtract what is already there
hook: Seven in stock and twelve needed: how many are missing?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Calculate nonnegative replenishment after counting available stock.

misconception: A shopping requirement is always the quantity that must be ordered.
objective: Calculate nonnegative replenishment after counting available stock.

claims.text: Seven usable units are already available. A orders only the gap; B orders the whole requirement. Scaled model; usable stock=7; no hidden commitments.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Required=12, A=5items and B=12items. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-","x",7]]; B="x"; x denotes Required. At x=12, A=5, B=12; recall at x=15: B=15. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Required quantity minus available stock gives the shortage. The maximum with zero prevents a negative order when stock already covers demand. Existing usable units belong in the calculation.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-","x",7]]; B="x"; x denotes Required. At x=12, A=5, B=12; recall at x=15: B=15. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: Seven usable units are already available. A orders only the gap; B orders the whole requirement. Change only Required to 15. What is B (Ignore-stock) now? Correct: 15items. Use B's stated rule with Required=15: it gives 15items. Required quantity minus available stock gives the shortage. The maximum with zero prevents a negative order when stock already covers demand. Existing usable units belong in the calculation.

At x=12, A=5, B=12; recall at x=15: B=15. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

recall.question: Seven usable units are already available. A orders only the gap; B orders the whole requirement. Change only Required to 15. What is B (Ignore-stock) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Required=15: it gives 15items. Required quantity minus available stock gives the shortage. The maximum with zero prevents a negative order when stock already covers demand. Existing usable units belong in the calculation.

safety.assumptions: Seven usable units are already available. A orders only the gap; B orders the whole requirement.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
